resources.string: Recovery, CPU, speaker timing, audio buffering and transfers
Saved changes apply to the next recording/session, model reload or download. An active operation keeps its starting snapshot. Reset affects only these runtime options.
Edit related fields together, then apply the group. Cancel discards the draft. Invalid combinations cannot be saved. Enter decimals with a dot.
Enter a whole number from %1$s to %2$s.
Enter a finite number from %1$s to %2$s.
Minimum must not exceed maximum; maximum plus both contexts must fit within 12 s.
Cache must be a multiple of 8; update frames must not exceed FIFO frames.
Next-operation configuration: ASR %1$d threads, diarization %2$d threads, ASR window %3$s s, queue budget %4$d s.

Compiled capability: CPU only. Fixed model/transport limits: 16 kHz mono PCM, 8 speaker output heads and a maximum 12 s audio window including context. These are not tuning options. Speaker identities can remain pending while future diarization labels arrive.

Connection limits waiting for the worker. Preparation and inference watchdogs measure time without progress, not total job length. Absolute timeout caps the whole operation even if it is progressing. Each accepts 0 to disable, or 1–86400 s. These are separate from idle model unloading, which releases models only between operations.

Thread counts are 0–32. Auto (0) uses the smaller of 4 and the available CPU count. Larger counts can increase heat and contention rather than improve speed. Model thread changes take effect on reload.

Latency presets trade future context for earlier labels; they do not change ASR windows. Native lookahead, chunk scheduling and label stabilization may delay speaker assignment beyond a window. Batch is 1–16; the measured default is 8. Use 1 for the strict native schedule when comparing accuracy. Activity threshold and winner margin are 0–1: increasing them makes attribution more conservative. Confirmation requires sustained evidence; bridging fills short unknown gaps; lookahead delays labels for future evidence; alignment tolerance allows timestamp uncertainty. Each timing is 0–10000 ms; 0 removes that allowance.

Strong activity and margin accept 0–1. Each effective value is max(ordinary, strong), so ordinary thresholds remain floors. Strong confirmation accepts 0–10000 ms and uses min(ordinary, strong); it never waits longer than ordinary confirmation. Both durations round up to 10 ms model frames, with a one-frame minimum. Ordinary confirmation 0 means one frame with no extra wait. The inferred word interval cap accepts 10–2000 ms and clips to the audio window; native end timings take precedence. These controls affect attribution, not ASR words or text ownership. New speech-island backfill requires a fully retained silent lookback of max(twice the unknown-gap bridge, alignment tolerance) before using the following voice.

Minimum window must not exceed maximum. Windows are 0.001–12 s; left/right context can be 0–12 s, but maximum window plus both contexts must fit within 12 s. Silence duration (1–60000 ms) and PCM16 amplitude (1–32767) guide segment boundaries. Queue budget caps accepted audio in memory at 1–300 s. A separate block-count bound can stop unusually small partial reads earlier. Overflow stops capture and drains accepted audio rather than silently dropping it; changes never resize a running queue.

Recorder buffer is 0.05–10 s and is always at least the Android minimum. Read blocks are 1–200 ms (up to 3200 samples). After waking, drain buffered audio before reopening a stalled microphone. Recovery grace and post-reopen grace are each 1–60000 ms. Android sleep/idle restrictions still defer recovery; a second failed recovery ends capture and preserves accepted audio.

Connection and read inactivity timeouts apply to the next download, consistently across all its files. Use 0 to disable or 1–86400 s. Read timeout is not a total transfer deadline. Cancellation and checksum verification remain active.

Cache is 16–1024 frames and must be a multiple of 8. FIFO is 16–1024 frames. Update is 1–FIFO frames; edit FIFO and update together. Smaller buffers can reduce context and accuracy. These are experimental runtime controls, not model dimensions. Diagnostics enables runtime timing information for troubleshooting.
